channel.description: Travel reporting, cultural heritage, and responsible exploration worldwide.

item.title: A Pirate’s Christmas in the Maldives: Kandooma Turns the Festive Season into an Island Adventure
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Kandooma Maldives, the festive season takes on an adventurous spirit, with a Pirates’ Festive Adventure programme running from December 22, 2026, through January 7, 2027. Set on a private island in the South Malé Atoll, the resort brings together Christmas and New Year celebrations with the pleasures of a tropical escape, from treasure-inspired activities at Kandoo Kids’ Club and Santa’s arrival to shark and turtle snorkeling, shipwreck safaris, sunset cruises and surfing lessons. Festive dining adds a distinctly Maldivian note, with traditional boduberu drumming, fire dancing, a Christmas Eve gala and New Year celebrations. Guests can also retreat to Kandooma Spa by COMO Shambhala for restorative treatments, while the resort’s experience-led all-inclusive offering combines dining, family activities and opportunities to explore the surrounding Indian Ocean. The programme continues through Orthodox Christmas, giving the season an extended island celebration.

The Curated Take

The Maldives is often associated with barefoot seclusion and overwater villas, but Kandooma offers a more active interpretation of the festive island escape. Its appeal lies in the range of experiences gathered into one setting: marine exploration for adventurous travelers, cultural performances and island flavors around the table, and dedicated activities that give families room to celebrate together. For those seeking a Christmas or New Year away from winter weather without sacrificing a sense of occasion, the combination of ocean adventure, wellness and Maldivian tradition makes for a spirited alternative to the usual holiday setting.

item.title: Napa Valley Gets a Winter Village of Its Own for the Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The holiday season takes on a distinctly Wine Country character at The Meritage Resort & Spa, where Merry Meritage returns November 19, 2026, through January 3, 2027, transforming the Napa Valley property into a vineyard-side winter village. Celebrating its 20th anniversary, the resort is introducing new experiences alongside returning seasonal traditions, including a holiday pop-up bar, interactive children’s activities, a weekend market featuring local vendors and expanded Princess Tinsel Teas. Guests can skate at Napa Valley’s largest outdoor ice rink, gather around fire pits for s’mores, visit Santa’s Workshop or enjoy sparkling high tea. New glass rinkside cabins offer a private setting for groups to take in the festivities, while nightly tree lighting and snowfall create a festive atmosphere across the property. From family-friendly celebrations to seasonal cocktails and intimate gatherings, Merry Meritage brings a winter holiday experience to California’s renowned wine region.

The Curated Take

There is something particularly appealing about a holiday escape that places seasonal traditions in an unexpected setting. Napa Valley is more often associated with vineyard landscapes, wine tasting and leisurely weekends, but Merry Meritage introduces another side of the destination, one shaped by winter festivities, culinary indulgence and the pleasure of gathering. The resort’s blend of outdoor skating, intimate fire pits, festive dining and local shopping gives the experience a sense of occasion without losing its Wine Country identity. For travelers looking to trade a traditional snowy getaway for a California holiday retreat, it offers a different kind of seasonal atmosphere.

item.title: Raleigh Makes a Compelling Case for a Culture-Focused Southern Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Raleigh, North Carolina, has earned its reputation as the “Smithsonian of the South,” bringing together internationally recognized collections, distinctive boutique museums and cultural experiences that invite visitors to look beyond the expected Southern city break. At the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences, guests can encounter the extraordinary Dueling Dinosaurs exhibition, observe active fossil research and explore one of the Southeast’s largest natural science collections. The North Carolina Museum of Art offers another remarkable draw, with the region’s largest Rodin sculpture collection and a 164-acre Museum Park that integrates monumental art installations with woodland trails. Beyond these major institutions, Raleigh’s cultural landscape extends to the historic City of Raleigh Museum, the interdisciplinary Gregg Museum of Art & Design, the interactive Marbles Kids Museum and the specialized Raleigh Lace Museum, where centuries of textile artistry are represented. With many of its museums offering free admission, Raleigh makes an especially inviting destination for travelers interested in art, science, history and the stories that give a city its character.

The Curated Take

A destination’s cultural identity is often revealed through more than its headline attractions. Raleigh’s strength is the range of discovery it offers, from internationally significant sculpture and rare paleontological collections to the intimate craftsmanship of lace-making. The combination of major museums and smaller, specialized institutions creates opportunities to move between grand collections and more personal encounters with art, history and local heritage. For culturally curious travelers, this is a city worth approaching with time to explore, particularly when its museums extend beyond traditional galleries into research spaces, university settings and expansive outdoor environments.

item.title: Puerto Vallarta’s Gourmet Festival Brings International Chefs to Three Velas Resorts
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The 31st edition of Festival Gourmet Internacional returns to Puerto Vallarta and Riviera Nayarit with more than 50 chefs and 25 participating restaurants, including special dining experiences at three Velas Resorts properties from November 13–22, 2026. At Grand Velas Riviera Nayarit, Colombian chef Andrés Fernándes León will present a six-course tasting menu inspired by French gastronomy and reinterpreted through Colombian ingredients and his own culinary perspective. Velas Vallarta welcomes Texas chef Victor Howard for a menu of smoked specialties, along with a hands-on cooking class and a beachside barbecue and wine celebration. At adults-only Casa Velas, Nahúm Velasco, Executive Chef of the MICHELIN-starred Cocina de Autor at Grand Velas Riviera Maya, will serve a six-course menu drawing on signature dishes and creations developed for the occasion. Together, the collaborations bring international culinary talent and regional interpretation to the resort experience.

The Curated Take

For travelers who plan their journeys around food, a festival like this offers more than a memorable dinner. It creates opportunities to encounter different culinary traditions through the perspectives of visiting chefs, while experiencing the distinct character of each resort. With events ranging from refined tasting menus to cooking classes and a sunset beach barbecue, Velas Resorts gives guests several ways to engage with Puerto Vallarta and Riviera Nayarit’s growing reputation as culinary destinations.

item.title: Christmas in November Returns to Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A beloved holiday tradition returns to the Canadian Rockies as Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge hosts Christmas in November from November 6–15, 2026. The adults-only celebration brings together acclaimed chefs, culinary demonstrations, tastings and seasonal workshops, alongside three signature evening events: the Evergreen Chalet welcome reception, Alpine Glow Dinner accompanied by The Aurora Ensemble, and the Northern Lights Ball featuring Canadian singer Nicolina Bozzo. New this year, the Fireside Reserve experience adds private culinary classes, an intimate cabin arrival, exclusive tastings and special gatherings with participating chefs and presenters. Between festivities, guests can take part in guided glacial plunges and wellness classes or simply enjoy the mountain setting and the resort’s reimagined spaces. The result is a festive escape that brings holiday spirit to the Rockies well before December.

The Curated Take

Christmas in November offers a different way to experience the holiday season, trading crowded December calendars for a multi-day celebration in the Canadian Rockies. Its appeal lies in the combination of culinary discovery, festive gatherings and time to reconnect with the surrounding landscape. For travelers who enjoy making the journey itself part of the holiday ritual, Jasper provides a particularly atmospheric setting for an early-season escape.

item.title: A More Intimate Way to Discover Europe: New Routes and Private Experiences for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Europe’s inland waterways offer a different perspective on some of the continent’s most storied regions, and European Waterways is expanding its 2027 luxury hotel barge collection with new itineraries and privately arranged cultural experiences. Among the additions is a journey through Brittany aboard the six-passenger Nymphea, tracing the River Oust and Canal de Nantes à Brest through medieval villages, historic châteaux and the region’s distinctive culinary landscape. In Burgundy, new visits to Château de Germolles and Château de Bazoches bring guests closer to medieval history through private falconry encounters, while the Canal du Midi itinerary introduces a tasting and private lunch at a family-owned wine and olive estate. Along Ireland’s River Shannon, guests can explore the heritage of Irish whiskey at Tullamore D.E.W. Distillery and the historic Birr Castle estate, including its remarkable scientific collections. With intimate vessels accommodating six to 20 guests, European Waterways combines gourmet dining, regional wines, personalized service and privately guided excursions for a slower, more immersive way to experience Europe.

The Curated Take

The appeal of hotel barging lies in its ability to make the journey itself part of the destination. Rather than moving quickly between Europe’s familiar landmarks, guests encounter smaller villages, family estates, historic residences and regional traditions at a more considered pace. The new experiences for 2027 add depth to that proposition, particularly through access that feels personal rather than transactional. A private encounter at a château, lunch among the vineyards or a closer look at Ireland’s scientific heritage can offer a richer understanding of a region than simply passing through it. For travelers drawn to cultural discovery, exceptional food and the intimacy of small-ship travel, Europe’s waterways remain an especially compelling way to explore.

item.title: A Taste of the Australian Summer Arrives at Park Hyatt Sydney with a Tim Tam Afternoon Tea
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
An Australian favorite gets a seasonal reinvention at Park Hyatt Sydney, where the hotel is bringing back its Tim Tam Afternoon Tea in collaboration with the iconic chocolate biscuit brand. Running from December 4, 2026, through February 28, 2027, the experience puts a distinctly Australian spin on the traditional afternoon tea, pairing familiar flavors with polished pastry craftsmanship and summer ingredients. Sweet selections include a mango and cream pavlova, an Iced Vovo-inspired éclair with raspberry and coconut, a chocolate and caramel biscuit creation, and a peach and rose roll. Savory offerings range from chicken and tarragon sandwiches to pork and fennel sausage rolls and chicken liver parfait brioche, alongside traditional scones and malt and vanilla cream beignets served with Tim Tam spread. Three festive drinks extend the collaboration, including a Tim Tam-inspired espresso martini and a non-alcoholic Iced Vovo mocktail. The result is a playful expression of Australian food culture in one of Sydney’s most celebrated luxury hotel settings.

The Curated Take

Afternoon tea has long been a ritual of elegant hotels, but its most memorable interpretations often reflect a sense of place. At Park Hyatt Sydney, the collaboration draws on a familiar Australian treat and gives it a new context through seasonal ingredients, inventive pastry and a distinctly local sense of fun. For international visitors, it offers a delicious introduction to a homegrown favorite; for Sydney locals, a reason to revisit a classic hotel ritual with a fresh perspective. Sometimes, a destination’s character is best discovered through something as simple as what is served at the table.

item.title: This Midwest City Is Earning a Place on the World’s Travel Bucket List for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Madison, Wisconsin, is stepping into the international travel spotlight after being named one of National Geographic’s Best of the World destinations for 2027, joining a global collection of cultural landmarks, outdoor escapes and emerging travel experiences. Wisconsin’s capital offers a distinctive blend of urban outdoor adventure, culinary discovery and creative culture, with its location between lakes Mendota and Monona shaping much of the city’s character. More than 200 miles of bicycle paths, abundant parks and accessible waterfront spaces make it easy to balance city exploration with time outdoors, while the historic Dane County Farmers’ Market, one of the largest producers-only farmers’ markets in the United States, offers a taste of the region’s agricultural and culinary traditions. Madison’s food scene has also earned national recognition, with 47 James Beard Award nominations to date and a growing collection of restaurants, bars and neighborhood gathering places. Cultural highlights include Olbrich Botanical Gardens, live music venues, independent businesses and the forthcoming Madison Public Market. For travelers seeking an American city break with a strong sense of place, Madison brings together lakefront scenery, farm-to-table dining, sustainability and a creative local identity in a refreshingly approachable Midwestern destination.

The Curated Take

Madison’s recognition is a reminder that compelling travel experiences are not always found in the world’s most obvious destinations. Its appeal comes from the relationship between the city and its natural surroundings, where lakeside recreation, farmers’ markets, culinary traditions and cultural spaces are woven into everyday life. For travelers interested in exploring beyond the familiar American city escapes, Madison offers an opportunity to experience the Midwest through its food, outdoor culture and independent spirit. Its National Geographic recognition makes 2027 an especially timely year to discover what gives this lakeside capital its character.

item.title: Orlando’s Holiday Season Shines Beyond the Theme Parks
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Orlando is welcoming the 2026 holiday season with an expansive calendar of festive experiences, from new attractions and immersive light displays to elegant hotel celebrations and neighborhood traditions. Across the destination, Universal Orlando Resort is extending its seasonal celebrations into the new Epic Universe, while LEGOLAND Florida introduces a Christmas drone show featuring LEGO Santa. Returning highlights include Walt Disney World’s holiday festivities and Dazzling Nights at Harry P. Leu Gardens, where illuminated landscapes and new performance elements create an immersive evening experience. Beyond the major attractions, downtown Orlando will host a free Frontyard Holiday Festival with nightly snowfall, live entertainment and a European-inspired holiday market, while ette hotel is partnering with Orlando Ballet for a Nutcracker-themed afternoon tea. At Evermore Orlando Resort, Grande Lakes, Four Seasons Resort Orlando and Conrad Orlando, seasonal programming adds another dimension to the destination’s holiday appeal. From family celebrations to sophisticated dining and festive resort escapes, Orlando offers a wide-ranging approach to winter travel in a destination known for its warm-weather setting.

The Curated Take

Orlando’s holiday appeal extends well beyond its reputation as a theme park destination. The breadth of seasonal programming reveals a more layered holiday escape, where immersive entertainment can be balanced with cultural performances, illuminated gardens, distinctive dining and resort experiences. For travelers seeking a winter celebration without the cold-weather setting, the destination offers considerable variety, whether the occasion calls for a multigenerational family gathering, a festive weekend away or a longer holiday stay. The most interesting additions are those that bring a sense of place to the season, from the Nutcracker-inspired tea to the downtown carillon and neighborhood celebrations.

item.title: Americans Are Rethinking Holiday Travel as Spending Concerns Rise
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
American holiday travel plans are showing signs of a slowdown, according to the latest Longwoods International tracking study, with more travelers expecting to cut back on both trips and spending in 2026. The October survey found that 31% of American travelers plan to travel less this holiday season than they did last year, an increase of eight percentage points from 2025 and 13 points from 2024. Meanwhile, 35% expect to spend less on holiday travel, up 11 points from the previous year, while only 16% anticipate traveling more and 22% expect to increase their spending. The broader outlook is also softening: the share of Americans with travel plans for the next six months has declined from 93% a year ago to 86%. Inflation and gasoline prices remain significant considerations, cited by 35% of respondents as major influences on their travel decisions. The survey, conducted October 6–9 among 1,000 U.S. adults, suggests that economic pressures are increasingly shaping how Americans approach the holiday travel season, although changes in fuel prices, airfares and consumer confidence could still influence demand.

The Curated Take

The findings point to a holiday season in which travel decisions may be less about abandoning travel altogether and more about reassessing its cost and value. For the luxury travel industry, that distinction matters. Travelers who remain committed to meaningful experiences may become more selective about where they go, how long they stay and what makes a journey worth the investment. Destinations and hospitality brands will need to communicate value beyond the rate itself, emphasizing distinctive experiences, thoughtful service and the reasons a trip deserves a place in the holiday budget. The coming months will reveal whether this early softness becomes a broader pullback or a more deliberate approach to travel spending.
